title: The .michi file format and the michi binary
body: Design agreed 2026-10-08 and recorded in docs/file-format.md. syntax.michi at the project root is the worked example. The parser comes first, then highlighting, then the CLI.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/a556920e
Jack Roddy/a556920e
Jack Roddy/a556920e
notes.text:
Design: lexical rules. Agreed 2026-10-08.

Newlines mean nothing anywhere. A statement ends at `;` or at a block.

- `//` starts a comment to end of line, outside command text only.
- Strings are double quoted. Raw strings are `r#"…"#` and carry no escapes.
- Numbers are bare: `8`, `7.5`. A duration is a number with a unit suffix,
  one of `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`: `30s`, `500ms`, `1h`. No compound forms.
- A bare identifier names an enum variant, in snake case: `spread`,
  `first_touch`, `on_failure`.
- Reserved words, which no name or data key may use: `data`, `pipeline`,
  `step`, `let`, `def`, `fn`, `for`, `in`, `if`, `else`, `use`, `import`,
  `include`, `true`, `false`. Only the first three mean anything yet.
- A dotted path, `quick.N`, names a value in a data block.
- `$N` names a sweep variable.
- A shebang on line one, `#!/usr/bin/env michi`, is skipped.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/a556920e
notes.text:
Design: files, data blocks and pipelines. Agreed 2026-10-08.

A file holds data blocks and one or more pipelines, in any order.

```
data NAME {
    X = [5, 10, 15];
    Y = "tmp/err";
}
```

A data block names a group of lists and scalars. A block at the top of the
file is visible to every pipeline in it, one inside a pipeline only there.
Two blocks of one name in one scope is an error. A value is referenced by
path, `NAME.X`, in any value position, and a scalar also in command text
as `${NAME.X}`, which is not valid shell and so cannot collide with it.

A list holds numbers, identifiers, strings, tuples, and ranges. A range is
one element and splices among the others:

| form | gives |
| --- | --- |
| `0..5` | 0 1 2 3 4 |
| `0..=5` | 0 1 2 3 4 5 |
| `0..100:5` | 0 5 10 … 95 |
| `1..=16:*2` | 1 2 4 8 16 |
| `0.0..=1.0:0.1` | 0.0 0.1 … 1.0 |
| `[1, 2, 4..=8, 16]` | 1 2 4 5 6 7 8 16 |

michi computes a float range as `start + i × step`, so it reaches the end
by count and not by accumulation, and it prints each value with as many
decimal places as the step or the start has, whichever is more, so `0.1`
steps print `0.3` and never `0.30000000000000004`. A literal float prints
as written.

```
#[pool(8)]
pipeline NAME { … }
```

A pipeline holds data blocks, steps and parameter-list blocks. Its
attributes are the pipeline builder's methods. A parameter list may not
wrap a pipeline.
